task.description: Validate src/design/iss0617-gbl134-missing-tables-followup.md, which designs a NEW forward migration GBL-136 to complete GBL-134's incomplete GLOBAL_REGISTRY table drop (13 missing table names, listed in the design). This is a database migration touching a table set already affected by ISS-0620's separate data-loss finding -- scrutinize carefully. Verify: (1) the exact 13-name list matches docs/issue-reports/ISS-0185-diagnosis.yaml's classification precisely -- cross-check yourself, do not trust the design doc's transcription; (2) the 4 ISS-0620-flagged names (artifact_activation_groups, entity_definitions, entity_record_latest, entity_type_instances) are genuinely absent from GBL-136's table list; (3) the FK-dependency analysis is correct -- independently query pg_constraint (or read the relevant table-creation migrations) to confirm artifact_versions genuinely has live FK dependents from PER_TENANT tables (artifact_activations, artifact_activation_history) that make it permanently un-droppable via RESTRICT, and confirm tenant_hostnames -> tenant is the only in-scope-to-in-scope dependency requiring drop ordering; (4) the exception-handling design (wrapping each drop in its own BEGIN...EXCEPTION WHEN dependent_objects_still_exist...END so one un-droppable table doesn't abort the whole migration) is a genuine, necessary deviation from GBL-134's bare structure -- confirm GBL-134's original pattern really would abort the whole transaction on a RESTRICT failure (read GBL-134's actual DO $$ block structure to confirm no existing exception handling); (5) the flagged GBL-135 discrepancy (claims 5 names reclassified PER_TENANT with public copies dropped, but design says live inspection shows all 5 public copies still exist) -- verify this claim yourself too, since if true it may need its own incidental-discovery filing (do not file it yourself, just confirm/deny it exists so ORCH can decide); (6) confirm no production code or test files are touched -- this should be pure migration design.
acceptance_criteria: The 13-name table list independently verified correct against the diagnosis file
ISS-0620s 4 flagged names confirmed absent from GBL-136s scope
FK-dependency analysis (artifact_versions un-droppable, tenant_hostnames->tenant ordering) independently verified against pg_constraint or source, not trusted
Exception-handling deviation from GBL-134s pattern confirmed necessary (not a fabricated justification)
GBL-135 discrepancy claim independently checked (confirm or deny, do not file anything)
No production code or test files touched

result.summary: Design src/design/iss0617-gbl134-missing-tables-followup.md is mostly correct but contains one confirmed factual error in its own acceptance/verification narrative, which is a BLOCKER-level design defect for a migration touching an already-sensitive table set (ISS-0620). VERIFIED CORRECT: (1) 13-name list -- independently computed set-difference of docs/issue-reports/ISS-0185-diagnosis.yaml's global_registry_tenant_default_is_stray list against GBL-134's actual v_tables array matches the design's 13 names exactly. (2) ISS-0620's 4 names (artifact_activation_groups, entity_definitions, entity_record_latest, entity_type_instances) confirmed absent from GBL-136's scope -- these are exactly the 'extra' 4 names in GBL-134's array not present in the diagnosis's GLOBAL list, confirming both the design's exclusion and ISS-0620's own finding independently. (3) FK-dependency claims for artifact_versions, tenant, tenant_hostnames, repository_artifacts, oidc_migration_item/job all confirmed correct via live pg_constraint queries against r-co-2-db_test-1/bpm_test. One additional undocumented FK dependent found: tenant_default.repository_form_schemas.version_id -> artifact_versions (fk_form_schema_version) -- this table is not in the ISS-0185 diagnosis at all and only exists in tenant_default (not public), so it does not change GBL-136's scope, but it reinforces (does not undermine) Section 3.1's conclusion that artifact_versions is permanently un-droppable via RESTRICT. MINOR: design's FK table in Section 3 is incomplete, should list this edge too. (4) Exception-handling deviation confirmed genuinely necessary -- GBL-134's DO $$ block (grep for BEGIN/EXCEPTION) has only its one outer BEGIN, no inner exception handler, so an unhandled dependent_objects_still_exist would abort the entire DO block and roll back all prior successful drops in the same file. GBL-136's per-table BEGIN...EXCEPTION WHEN dependent_objects_still_exist...END wrapper is a real, warranted structural deviation, not fabricated. (5) GBL-135 DISCREPANCY CLAIM -- CONFIRMED, BUT THE DESIGN'S CONCLUSION IS BACKWARDS. Design Section 5 claims 'live inspection shows all 5 public copies still exist' for api_token_audit, event_payload_store, instance_definition_snapshots, instance_waits, variable_schemas. Direct live query against bpm_test (docker exec r-co-2-db_test-1 psql) shows the OPPOSITE: NONE of these 5 tables exist in public schema anymore -- schema_migrations confirms GBL-135 has already run, and GBL-135's ACTUAL v_tables array (not just its stale header comment) literally includes all 5 names, so GBL-135 already dropped their public copies. This means GBL-136's Defense 1 (only drop if table also exists in public) will SILENTLY SKIP all 5 names as no-ops when GBL-136 runs -- their tenant_default shadow copies will NOT be dropped. This directly contradicts the design's own Section 8 verification query, which lists these 5 names among the set expected to return 0 rows in tenant_default after GBL-136 runs; that verification would FAIL for all 5. Root cause: the diagnosis file itself double-classifies these 5 names (present in BOTH global_registry_tenant_default_is_stray AND per_tenant_public_is_stray lists), and GBL-135 already resolved the conflict operationally in the PER_TENANT direction before this design was written, but the design's Section 5 author verified against stale information. INCIDENTAL FINDING (not filed by validator per instructions): the diagnosis file's own list labels are internally inconsistent -- global_registry_tenant_default_is_stray is labeled ':37' but actually lists 33 items; per_tenant_public_is_stray is labeled ':8' but actually lists 13 items; 33+13=46, not the stated total_classified:45. This pre-existing inconsistency does not affect the 13-name computation (verified via direct set-difference of actual list contents, not the mislabeled counts) but should be flagged for its own incidental-discovery issue. (6) Confirmed no production code or test files touched -- diff vs origin/main on this branch touches only the design doc and workflow bookkeeping files. tools/lint_design_artefact.py exits 0, BLOCKER=0 MAJOR=0 MINOR=4 (schema-qualification style notes only).

issues.description: Section 5's core factual claim is backwards: live inspection of bpm_test shows api_token_audit, event_payload_store, instance_definition_snapshots, instance_waits, and variable_schemas have ALREADY had their public copies dropped by GBL-135 (confirmed both by direct psql query returning 0 rows for all 5 in public, and by GBL-135's actual v_tables array containing all 5 names -- not just its header comment). The design asserts the opposite ('all 5 public copies still exist'). Consequence: GBL-136's Defense 1 guard (only drop if table exists in public) will cause these 5 names to be silently skipped as no-ops, so their tenant_default shadow copies will remain un-dropped. This directly contradicts the design's own Section 8 verification query, which asserts these 5 names should return 0 rows in tenant_default after GBL-136 runs -- that assertion will fail. Needs rework: either (a) design a path to drop these 5 tables' tenant_default copies despite their public copies already being gone (would require relaxing or special-casing Defense 1 for exactly these 5, with its own safety analysis), or (b) explicitly exclude these 5 from GBL-136's scope with documented rationale and correct the Section 8 verification query and the 13-name claim/count accordingly, or (c) resolve the underlying double-classification conflict in the diagnosis file first. Must not proceed to BACKEND-DEV with a design whose own acceptance criteria are known-fail before implementation starts, especially on a table set already implicated in ISS-0620's BLOCKER-severity data-loss finding.

Section 3's FK-dependency table for artifact_versions is incomplete: live pg_constraint inspection found an additional dependent not listed, tenant_default.repository_form_schemas.version_id -> artifact_versions (fk_form_schema_version). Does not change the design's conclusion (artifact_versions remains permanently un-droppable via RESTRICT, now for one more reason), so this does not block PASS on its own, but should be added to the table for completeness when the design is reworked for the BLOCKER above.

Incidental finding, not to be filed by this validator per task instructions: docs/issue-reports/ISS-0185-diagnosis.yaml's classification_table has internally inconsistent counts -- global_registry_tenant_default_is_stray is labeled ':37' but the YAML list under it has 33 items; per_tenant_public_is_stray is labeled ':8' but has 13 items; 33+13=46 items total against a stated total_classified:45. Also directly relevant to the BLOCKER above: 5 table names appear in BOTH lists simultaneously (api_token_audit, event_payload_store, instance_definition_snapshots, instance_waits, variable_schemas), a genuine double-classification, not just a counting error. ORCH should consider routing this to ISSUE-FIXER as its own incidental-discovery filing.
